about: The repair list (tools/repairs.ps1 describes the fields and writes docs/axKit/repairs.md from this file). Started by the audit of 2026-11-13: seven independent read-only reviews of the code, the tests and tooling, the documents and the last five days of changes, each finding checked against the code before it was entered.

principles.name: Say the effect where the thing is made
principles.text: Whoever makes a menu item, a command or a run states what it does and what it acts on; nothing important rests on a default. What states nothing is treated as the most careful case.

principles.name: One source, generated views
principles.text: A fact lives in one place (the menu bar, Dispatch.Apps, a JSON list); every page or list that repeats it is written by a script and checked by the same gate on the developer's computer and in CI.

principles.name: A failure says what, why and where to read
principles.text: Every refusal, error and failed check names the thing, the reason and the document or command that helps; nothing fails silently and nothing passes silently against the wrong thing.

principles.name: Bounded and cleaned up
principles.text: Every wait has a limit, every held resource is released on every path (try/finally), every input from outside has a size limit.

principles.name: An entry is its name, never a held object
principles.text: What is found in one moment and used in another (a menu item, a file, a selection) is found again by its identity when it is used, and refused when it is gone or changed.

principles.name: Writes are whole or not at all
principles.text: A file a user or the app depends on is written through a temporary file and put in place in one step; an undo step is dropped only once it has been applied.

principles.name: Tests check the built thing
principles.text: What matters is checked on the running window or the built data; a test that reads source text is lint, a help and never the proof.

principles.name: Documents describe the present
principles.text: Reference text says what is true now, in small files a reader with little context can hold; history lives in the changelog and git; open work lives in the priorities list.

items.title: Recent folders of axClaude and axTerminal started Claude Code or a shell for an AI tool without asking

items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/AutomationEnvironmentTests; every tests/scripts run still starts

items.title: The pairing Deny cool-down and the rate limit live in the broker, which a client can start again

items.verify: tests/scripts/mcp/01-read-and-pair.txt, a second broker after Deny
items.note: Declined 2026-11-13: that a new session of a client is asked again is the design (MC-6.4, held by tests/scripts/mcp/01-read-and-pair.txt): a user who denied by mistake restarts the client to be asked. The question is unprompted with Deny as default and a moment in which keys do nothing, so a client that restarts its broker gains a repeated question, never an answer.

items.verify: tests/scripts/axHelp/01-start.txt hears it

Since 2026-11-15 the receiving window also takes a hand-over only from a sender that names a window of this very program file (AppMessage.SenderRefusal, every verb): a program that only knows the message is refused, but a program running as the user can name a window not its own, so the words stay said.

items.fix: One record per item in one table (MenuItemInfo: its mark, withheld, left out, its refreshes as a list); Tag is no longer used for menus.

items.title: Reading the entries rebuilt a menu the user had open, and listed placeholders that do nothing
items.fix: A menu whose list is showing is read as it stands; the placeholder of an empty list is left out of the entries.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/CommandPaletteTests

items.title: The one command list is not one: items are made by Add(Command), by Item() and by bare ToolStripMenuItem
items.fix: In steps, one app per commit: (1) ItemForm's shared actions become Command records the apps place with Add; (2) Item() becomes private to the base; (3) each app's static raw items become commands, its filled lists state a mark; (4) the test counts every item made without a mark and its limit falls to zero.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/CommandMarkTests' count falls with each step; every tests/scripts folder of the app passes
items.note: About 131 items in the apps and 28 in the base state no mark (they ask before an AI tool runs them; safe, but a question more than needed, and their menu path is not in the report's recent actions). docs/axKit/app-kit.md AK-2 describes MenuSpec, Scope and Help, which do not exist: the document follows the code in the same steps. Settled 2026-11-13: all 160 judged and marked; Item(text, action, key, mark) with the mark required; items filled as a menu opens wrapped in CommandPalette.Marked; the empty-list lines NoEntry. Not done, by choice: ItemForm's shared actions stay AddKey commands with the apps' Context items beside them (the items now carry the same marks), since moving them would change every item app's menus for no gain a user or an AI tool would meet. docs/axKit/app-kit.md AK-2 says what is built.

items.title: A run for an AI tool could still execute after the client was told it timed out
items.fix: Run gives up as App does: a flag both threads swap, so a request not taken up in time never runs.
items.verify: reading against App(); tests/scripts/mcp
items.note: In OnWindow itself, so every request of the pipe has it; a timeout now answers in words the client can act on.

items.title: Menu refreshes read files on the window's thread at every palette opening and AI call
items.fix: The switches' states are read once per reading of the entries and cached for a second; the Window menu's lists likewise.
items.verify: a count of file reads per Entries call in CommandPaletteTests
items.note: The reads are of small files in the user's own settings folder, a few milliseconds, as every opening of these menus always did; rule 3 is about I/O that can block (a network, a program). Counted: three files per reading of the entries, at most ten readings a second from an AI tool (the rate limit). A cache would add stale checks to save nothing a user can perceive.

items.title: A notice shown over another replaces it and the replaced notice's cancel never runs
items.fix: ShowNotice runs the cancel of the notice it replaces, unless it is chained from that notice's own button.
items.verify: a script: the Hotkey notice replaced by an error, the hotkey then hides the window
items.note: Fixed where it bit, not in ShowNotice: running a replaced notice's cancel in general would break the notices that are replaced on purpose and come back (Find inside a notice). The hotkey capture now asks which notice is on view instead of trusting a flag. The rule for new code: state that outlives a notice is read from the notice showing, never from a flag its buttons clear.

items.title: AxKitForm is one class of about 3,400 lines in twelve files that every app inherits whole
items.fix: The services with their own state move out into plain classes the base holds (the updater flow, the installer, the report sender, AI help, the AI tools' window side), one per commit, the base keeping the hooks; no behaviour changes.
items.verify: every tests/scripts folder after each move
items.note: Done in part on 2026-11-14, one move per step, the window checks after each. Moved, each a plain sealed class the base makes in its constructor with the window as its one collaborator: UpdateFlow (the check, the offer, the install in place, the restart), ProgramInstaller (Install it now), ReportFlow (the report notice, the saving, the sending), AiHelpFlow (the switch, the question, the answer, the folders) and AiToolsSetup (what the AI tools submenu's items do, and the pairing notice). The base keeps the members an app calls, the menu items with their marks and every hook, unchanged; no app's code changed. Not moved, and why: the run of a command for an AI tool (McpRunCommand, AskToRunMcp, RunForMcp, McpAfterRun, with its ticket, the minute after a Deny and the chime's time) and the request list (ShowOfferedRequest, ShowOfferedRequestIn). Their fields are touched by AxKitForm.Mcp.cs alone, but the code reads and sets the window's notice, dialog, focus and menus in many places and calls three hooks (McpTarget, ShowOfferedRequest, NoticeChime): coupling to describe, not a service to cut, and the test of the order of focus and comparison in AskToRunMcp reads it where it is. Deferred for that part alone, until the agent window's shared layer says what it needs of it. The pattern is written in src/AxKit.Forms/notes/window-base.md, The services the window holds.

items.title: Only the settings were written through a temporary file; documents, items, the theme and the key were written in place
items.fix: One SafeFile.Write (a temporary file of its own name beside the target, then replaced in one step, the target's attributes kept) used by all five; the settings' fixed .tmp name, which two windows shared, goes.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/SafeFileTests; the editors' and axTask's scripts

items.title: The update signature covers the zip alone, not its version: an older signed release could be offered as a newer one
items.fix: The updater refuses a zip whose own version (read from the AxKit.exe inside it, after the signature holds) is not the version the release names and not newer than the one running.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/UpdaterTests with a zip of an older version
items.note: Needs no change to the signature format, so earlier releases still verify. Threat: the GitHub account taken over; the signing key stays offline. Updater.VersionRefusal, asked after the signature holds and the zip is extracted; UpdaterTests.

items.title: cmd.exe's special characters are checked in two callers that start a .cmd and missed in two
items.fix: One check in the one place that builds a command line for claude.cmd; a folder or argument with such a character is refused with the reason.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/SystemProgramsTests and AiTests, tests/AxClaude.Tests/ClaudeLauncherTests: both callers with a folder named R&D, and a real batch file run by cmd.exe
items.note: Done 2026-11-14: SystemPrograms.LineFor is the one command line for a program that may be a batch file, used by every start of Claude Code (session, version, AI help, the AI tools registration) through ClaudeCodeProgram.LineFor; a batch file gets every argument quoted and is refused a percent sign, an exclamation mark, a double quote or a line break with a sentence naming the character and the argument. Only the npm install (claude.cmd) was affected.

items.verify: tests/AxMCP.Tests
items.note: A batch program with an argument cmd.exe would act on is refused with the reason.

items.fix: A broken pipe while writing the input is not an error of the run: the outputs and the exit code are returned.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/ProcessRunTests

items.fix: Every text and pattern of Claude Code's moves into one table (ClaudeText), each with the Claude Code version it was last seen in and the fixture that shows it; a test fails on such a literal elsewhere in the project; tools/claude-text.ps1 writes the page that is compared when a new Claude Code version comes.

items.title: Smaller core items: PtyHost.Kill after Dispose, JsonDocument not disposed, a report posted before it is marked sent, the seal's unescaped separators, AppPaths' uneven test-run home
items.fix: Each fixed where it stands.

items.title: The local gate did not run the page checks that failed CI six times in three days
items.fix: test.ps1 ends with the three page checks (outside calls, workflows, repairs); release.ps1 writes all three pages before its commit; the outside-calls page names the file and function of a call, no line number, so an edit above a call no longer makes it stale.
items.verify: test.ps1 fails on a stale page; gh run list shows no page failure after it

items.title: CI runs no window script, and no document said so
items.fix: automation.md and the workflows page say that the window scripts run on the developer's computer (nvda-pass.ps1 and tools/AxAutomate), never in CI, and what CI does prove.
items.verify: reading

items.title: The runner drove whatever build lay in src\AxKit\bin\Release when none was named
items.fix: No default: --build or --exe is required; the console and the report's first lines give the program's version and when it was built; the exit codes are 0, 1 (a script failed), 2 (could not start).
items.verify: a run without either option ends with the message; the report's header
items.note: Cost two wrong diagnoses on 2026-11-13.

items.title: An NVDA run that ended abnormally left NVDA's speech capture on
items.fix: The run's end is a finally; every run deletes an earlier run's flag first; the add-on ignores a flag older than two hours.
items.verify: reading; nvda-pass.ps1 once
items.note: Privacy: the capture writes what NVDA speaks into a file. The add-on installed in NVDA is a copy: tools/nvda-capture is copied to %APPDATA%\nvda\addons\axkitCapture and NVDA restarted for the two-hour rule to hold there.

items.title: A window whose thread hung blocked a run forever, in the NVDA tier with the keyboard taken
items.fix: A read of the window's pipe waits 30 seconds at most and then fails the step, naming the window.
items.verify: tests/AxAutomate.Tests

items.title: Scripts that depend on a live model or the network read like any other when they fail
items.fix: A script says what it needs in its header (# Needs: Claude Code, the network, KeePassXC); the runner's summary and the workflows page give those apart, so a model's change of wording is not taken for a regression.
items.verify: tests/AxAutomate.Tests; the summary of a run
items.note: 257 fixed waits in 56 scripts stand in for conditions; each is replaced by an expectation when its script is next touched. Done: the # Needs: line on 29 scripts and on the workflows page. Open as part of R-37: the runner's summary giving such scripts apart, and the fixed waits.

items.title: Two scripts name KeePassXC by one computer's path, and one overwrites the user's clipboard
items.fix: The path comes from where the tool is found; the clipboard step saves and puts back what was there, or goes.
items.verify: the scripts pass
items.note: KeePassXC's place is stated as the scripts' need; the two scripts that write the clipboard on purpose are named in automation.md.

items.title: Tests that read source text can be passed by ordinary code they do not see
items.fix: The runner's check commands step, which every app's first script runs on the built window, also fails on a menu entry with no stated mark once R-11 is done; the text tests stay as lint and say so.
items.verify: check commands in each app's script
items.note: AxKitForm.CommandProblems fails on any entry of the built window that states no mark and is not withheld; the first full run found six items the source test could not see (Exit, Check for updates, Update to, Record raw stream, Hotkey, two empty-list lines). The source tests say they are lint.

items.title: Hygiene: release.ps1 can wait on CI forever; empty AxList folders; merged branches; two forgotten worktrees; tools/EdgeDrive in no solution
items.fix: A time limit on the wait; the empty folders removed; the branches and worktrees listed for the maintainer, who deletes branches himself.
items.verify: reading
items.note: Done: the empty AxList folders and two stale worktrees removed (both clean or holding only a generated page). The seventeen merged branches deleted by the maintainer on 2026-11-13, here and on GitHub. Open: the time limit on release.ps1's wait; the two unmerged branches cleanup and night-check, to be read and merged or dropped; tools/EdgeDrive is in no solution. 2026-11-13: release.ps1 asks for the build every 20 s, 40 minutes at most. The branches cleanup and night-check hold nothing main lacks (four commits already in main by content, one accidental commit of the lists hook, one merge of two merged branches): the maintainer deletes them with git branch -D. tools/EdgeDrive stays outside the solution by choice: a maintainer tool for Partner Center, built on its own.

items.title: axPass and axTask dropped an undo step before applying it: a failed undo lost it
items.fix: The step is looked at, applied, and removed only when the undo succeeded.
items.verify: tests/AxTask.Tests; reading for axPass
items.note: axPass fixed. axTask left as it is, on purpose: a step that can no longer be undone (its files changed since) is dropped so that the steps before it can still be reached, and says why.

items.title: Windows ask whether their last folder exists on the window's thread, without the local-drive guard
items.fix: One LocalPaths.ExistingOr(last, fallback) for the start-up folder, asking of a local path only.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/LocalPathsTests
items.note: A last folder on an unreachable share would stall the start. Kept as it is, on purpose. The guard that fits a menu (list a network path without asking) is wrong for a start: skipping a remembered folder because it is on a network drive would cost everyone who works on one their folder at every start, to spare a wait that only comes when the share cannot be reached and that Windows bounds. The right fix, if it is ever reported, is the start-up check off the window's thread, one app at a time.

items.title: axPass reads an entry in an async void outside Do
items.fix: Through Do, so that any failure is a notice.
items.verify: tests/scripts/axPass
items.note: The read is a background convenience: its failures are logged, not shown, on purpose, and an exception outside the filter reaches the crash handler, which shows it as a notice in the window. A notice for every failed read would interrupt the user for nothing they asked for.

items.title: The same small piece written two or three times: one instance of a hotkey app, the busy guard and its words, the item apps' undo stack
items.fix: AppHost.OneInstance; one Busy helper in the base with one wording; the undo stack in ItemForm.
items.verify: the apps' scripts
items.note: With R-11, app by app. AppHost.FirstInstance replaces the three copies of the one-instance mutex. Left as they are, by choice: the busy guards of axGIT, axProcess and axPass hold different things (a verb for the status bar, a phrase in the list's name, a flag) in about ten lines each, and the item apps' undo stacks hold each app's own kind of step; one shared piece would need the generics rule B-10 rules out.

items.title: What a reader must hold to change one app is about 90,000 tokens; the root instructions alone are 31 KB of three paragraphs
items.fix: Root CLAUDE.md is the rules, the gotchas and pointers, 8 KB at most, the commands on a page of their own; the AxKit.Forms notes split by kind of window; reference text loses its dates and until-clauses.
items.verify: a size check in tools/docs-check.ps1
items.note: The root file is loaded into every session: it is rewritten in one commit of its own and read by the maintainer. Done 2026-11-13: the root CLAUDE.md from 32 KB to 14 KB, its long paragraphs moved whole into docs/axKit/commands.md, documents.md and the generated apps.md; the rules, the gotchas and the manual verification unchanged. Open: src/AxKit.Forms/CLAUDE.md (53 KB) split by kind of window, and the dates and until-clauses out of the reference text of the specs. 2026-11-13: src/AxKit.Forms/CLAUDE.md from 54 KB to a 3 KB index over src/AxKit.Forms/notes, one file per kind of window (NotesTests reads them). Declined: taking the dates and until-clauses out of the specifications. They record when a decision was made and by whom, which is what a reader needs when a rule is questioned; the load problem this finding named is met by the root file's 15 KB and the split notes.

items.title: Settings that name what is run are plain files nothing checks
items.fix: One seal in AxKit.Core, SettingsSeal (docs/axKit/SPEC.md AX-5.6): each settings class seals its run-deciding fields at every save; a field whose seal does not check is put to its default, not used, and the user is told once; a file from before the seal is accepted and sealed at its next save, and the files this install has sealed are listed with the key. McpAccess keeps its file, key and seal value and takes the HMAC from it. A custom shell's consent is for its command line; a repository's trust is for the programs it named.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/SettingsSealTests (the piece, AI help's settings, the consents, the AI tools' seal value); tests/AxTerminal.Tests/TerminalSealTests; tests/AxGit.Tests/GitSealTests; tests/AxMCP.Tests/MCPSealTests; tests/AxFile.Tests/FileSealTests; tests/AxClaude.Tests/SettingsSealTests; tests/scripts/axTerminal/08-user-shells and tests/scripts/axGIT/07-own-programs for the window; the refusal sentences in the windows are owed a hearing
items.note: Found on 2026-11-16 by the resilience audit. Every part is done: axTerminal's shell, custom command line and user shells, with the consent bound to the command line and the command line in the start line; AI help's switch, folders, claudePath and working folder, and axClaude's claudePath; consent.json; axGIT's trusted repositories, each with the SHA-256 of the names of what it would run, asked again when that differs; axMCP's servers and axFile's programs. The limit, written in SPEC AX-5.6, SECURITY.md and the guides: a program running as the user can ask Windows for the same key; the seal holds against a file edited by another program or by hand, a profile copied or synced from elsewhere, and an AI tool writing files. Left as open work: AI help's claudePath and workingFolder, and axClaude's claudePath while Claude Code is found, have no menu item, so once their file is sealed they cannot be changed by hand; a trust's mark is of the names of a repository's programs, not of what a hook's file holds.

items.title: Files Claude Code obeys in Claude's working folder are outside the self-repair
items.fix: Shift+F1's print mode runs Claude Code with --strict-mcp-config and --settings on a file of axKit's own that holds disableAllHooks, written again before each question (ai-help.md AH-2.6). Before axHelp starts its conversation, AiFolderCheck lists the obeyed files axKit did not write (.mcp.json, a hooks member of the folder's settings files, the files under .claude's skills, commands, output-styles, plugins, agents and rules but axKit's own), each with a SHA-256, and compares them with the list the user last accepted, kept under the settings' seal; a new or changed one is named in a notice in axHelp's window whose default is Cancel, and the start in the background does not happen in such a folder (AH-7.8, axHelp HE-2.9).
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/AiFolderCheckTests; tests/AxKit.Tests/AiTests (the command line, the file put right before a run); tests/AxHelp.Tests/HelpTests (A_working_folder_as_axHelp_prepares_it_holds_no_file_to_ask_about_and_a_changed_agent_is_one); owed: a live print-mode question with a hook and a .mcp.json in the folder (tools/upstream.ps1 -Verify), and a window check and a hearing of the notice, which no script reaches without a live Claude Code
items.note: Found on 2026-11-16 by the resilience audit. Checked against Claude Code's documentation and claude --help of 2.1.325 that day: print mode shows no trust question and obeys a folder's hooks and servers; --strict-mcp-config and --settings exist; --setting-sources user is not used, since it would drop the folder's rules, axKit's two among them. The JSON goes in a file because npm's claude.cmd is refused an argument with a double quote. By decision CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md are not on the list. Left open: an axClaude window started in that folder by the user is Claude Code's own trust question's; a running conversation is not checked again when brought up; settings members other than hooks that name a command (statusLine, apiKeyHelper) are not checked.

items.title: Report items planted in the reports folder go out with the user's next report
items.fix: axKit keeps the names of the report files its own form saved, under the settings' seal, written as each report is saved; the sender sends only waiting items on that list, leaves the others untouched and counts them, and what the window says after a send ends with how many were not sent (reports.md RP-6.9). No question is asked. Until the first report this version saves the list is not kept and the sender sends as before; that save takes the waiting reports onto the list; afterwards a deleted or refused list is empty.

items.title: git and PowerShell 7 are taken from the PATH before Program Files
items.fix: The install folders only an administrator can write come first, and PATH folders that are not local are passed over.
items.verify: tests/AxKit.Tests/SystemProgramsTests (An_installed_program_is_found_in_its_install_folder_before_the_path_and_never_in_a_path_folder_off_this_computer, The_install_folders_are_under_Program_Files_as_Windows_names_them); tests/AxGit.Tests and tests/AxTerminal.Tests still pass with the installed git and PowerShell; owed: a live start of axGIT and of PowerShell 7 in axTerminal on a computer where the program is installed for the user alone (found through the PATH)
items.note: Found on 2026-11-16 by the second reading. Read first, as asked: the agreements are for the program's name alone (the consent's targets are "Git" and "PowerShell 7"; only a custom shell's target holds its command line, R-53), the question's words name no path, and axTerminal's start line is "Shell started: PowerShell 7 in <folder>", again without the path; axGIT says no path of git anywhere. So nothing told the user which file ran, and the finding stands. git.exe and pwsh.exe are now looked for in Git\cmd and PowerShell\7 under Program Files and Program Files (x86), as Windows names those folders, before the PATH, and PATH folders that are not on a drive of this computer are passed over (SystemPrograms.Installed; SPEC AX-11.5; the same for the git.exe Git Bash is found beside and for a powershell.exe on the PATH). Left as they are: axMCP's servers and KeePassXC's tool are still found through the whole PATH (a server's agreement is for its resolved path, R-61; KeePassXC's tool must carry its publisher's signature, R-55).

items.title: axHelp's model setting reaches Claude Code's command line unchecked
items.fix: A model name is letters, digits, dots, hyphens and brackets, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is the default.
items.verify: tests/AxHelp.Tests/HelpTests (Only_a_models_name_is_kept_and_reaches_the_command_line)
items.note: Found on 2026-11-16 by the second reading. HelpSettings.IsModelName, the pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\[\]-]*$ with a hundred characters at most, checked at the load and once more where the command line is made; a refused value is the fast model, with its length in the log and nothing said (docs/axHelp/SPEC.md HE-2.3). Not touched: axClaude's own --model, which is the user's command line and passed on as typed.

items.title: A list's action keys in list.json are not checked
items.fix: An action key that opens or moves says what it now does and waits for a second press when the list's keys differ from the ones this install wrote or accepted.
items.verify: tests/AxTask.Tests/ActionKeysTests (A_key_that_moves_or_opens_asks_first_and_one_that_sets_fields_does_not, An_acceptance_is_for_one_list_one_key_and_one_action_and_is_kept_under_the_seal, The_acceptances_are_kept_to_a_limit_the_oldest_going_first); tests/scripts/axTask/04-action-keys for the window (the first press says, the second does, the third acts at once); owed: a hearing with NVDA (nvda-test-plan section 5, step 5a)
items.note: Found on 2026-11-16 by the second reading: a shared or rewritten list. The words: "Ctrl+2 in this list now moves to ../Later. Press it again to do it." The seal is per list and key, not per list: an acceptance is the bundle's seal (SettingsSeal.Of) over the list's folder, the digit and the action, kept in axTask's settings as acceptedActionKeys, so that accepting one key says nothing of the eight others the user has not heard (docs/axTask/SPEC.md TK-7a.3). A key written in Actions, Action keys is accepted as it is written. Left open: every move or open key of a list made before this version asks once; a key set in the form and then taken back by Ctrl+Z stays accepted.

items.title: A window started as a test run looks like the user's own
items.fix: Such a window's title says that it is a test run.
items.note: Declined on 2026-11-16 under the boundary the user set that day: axKit answers for what axKit does, and a program that can start AxKit.exe with a home and a secret of its own choosing already runs as the user and can do anything the user can. A mark in the title would also cost 64 pinned titles in 26 scripts and the exact-title lookups of the background apps. Found on 2026-11-16 by the second reading, plausible: any program can start the exe with a secret and a home folder of its own choosing. Left open on 2026-11-16 after reading how a title is made: 26 scripts of tests/scripts pin 64 whole titles ("title":"..." with its closing quote), each of which ", test run" at the end would change, and the title is more than a label: a second start of axStart, axClip, axHelp and of axHelp's conversation finds the running window by its exact title (BundleWindows.Titled), and titles are set in four kinds of place (AxKitForm.SetTitle, ConsoleForm, HotkeyForm and the windows' own UpdateTitle). So the words in the title mean either editing those 26 scripts or making a test run's windows look themselves up differently from the user's, which is the code the scripts are there to check. A way that changes no title is to be chosen first, for example the words in the window's accessible description or as the first thing a test run's window says.
